reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not support the key premises. E1 describes a thick, hard AlBeSiTiV coating on steel, which is unrelated to the proposed ductile CoCrFeNi coating, its deposition method, residual stress state, or effect on caloric properties. E2 describes magnetron sputtering of CoCrFeNi films on sapphire, but provides no information on graded layers, residual stresses, mechanical integrity enhancement, or caloric performance preservation. The premises thus lack specific prior evidence.
premises: A thin, ductile, nanocrystalline CoCrFeNi-based coating can be deposited via DC magnetron sputtering with a graded adhesion layer.
The coating will impose beneficial compressive residual stresses and blunt crack initiation.
The coating will enhance load-bearing integrity without altering the bulk crystallography.
The limited coating thickness will preserve the bulk phase transformation and caloric response.
The coating will remain adherent and effective under cyclic magnetic, pressure, and thermal loading.
